overview: Build fluency in core roofing terminology and materials. Learn components, flashing types, shingle categories, and damage language so you can communicate clearly with homeowners and adjusters.
learningObjectives: Identify and define 25+ essential roofing terms
Distinguish shingle types and materials (architectural vs. 3‑tab vs. specialty)
Recognize roof components and explain their functions
Use proper terminology with homeowners and adjusters

sections.title: Essential Roofing Terminology
sections.content: Shingles (overlapping covering), Decking/Sheathing (plywood/OSB base), Underlayment (water‑resistant barrier), Ice & Water Shield (self‑adhering leak protector), Flashing (metal water diversion), Ridge (horizontal peak), Hip (external angle), Valley (internal angle), Eave (lower overhang), Rake (sloped gable edge), Soffit (underside of overhang), Fascia (vertical edge board).

sections.title: Flashing Types
sections.content: Step Flashing (roof‑to‑wall), Counter/Apron Flashing (covers step), Drip Edge (edge water control), Pipe Boot (penetration seal).

sections.title: Shingle Types and Materials
sections.content: Architectural: dimensional, multi‑layer. English vs. Metric: exposure differences; don’t mix. 3‑Tab: flat, uniform, shorter lifespan. Specialty: designer/premium, impact‑resistant, solar‑reflective.

sections.title: Damage Identification Terms
sections.content: Hail: granule loss, impact marks, exposed mat, fractures. Wind: uplift, creasing, tearing, seal failure. Collateral: soft metals, screens, siding.
